skill.name: performance-analysis
skill.description: Analyzes Claude Flow swarm performance, detects bottlenecks, and recommends targeted optimizations.
skill.summary: Analyze Claude Flow swarm metrics, bottlenecks, and optimization opportunities.
skill.author: Claude Flow Team

security_audit.summary: Static alerts were reviewed against SKILL.md and most are false positives from fenced Markdown examples, inline option names, documentation links, and a hardcoded sample script. I found no prompt injection, credential access, network exfiltration, or malicious hidden behavior. A semantic concern remains because the skill promotes --fix workflows that can change Claude Flow swarm behavior without documenting an approval or rollback step.

remediation.issue: Automatic fix mode can change swarm configuration or runtime behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit confirmation, dry-run, backup, and rollback guidance before recommending --fix on active swarms.

remediation.issue: The custom script example uses child_process.exec.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer execFile or spawn with fixed argument arrays, and state that user input must never be passed into shell commands.

remediation.issue: Documentation links include absolute workspace paths.
remediation.suggestion: Replace absolute /workspaces/.claude links with package-relative documentation links for portability and reduced path disclosure.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Fix Mode Can Change Swarm Behavior
semantic_findings.description: The skill encourages --fix usage and says automatic optimizations may change topology, caching, concurrency, priorities, and resource behavior. These changes are operationally sensitive and should require explicit approval and rollback guidance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited prose directly documents auto-fix commands and the classes of changes applied. It is a safety risk, not evidence of malicious intent, so confidence is high but severity remains medium.

content.value_statement: Claude Flow swarms can slow down when bottlenecks are hidden across agents, memory, and coordination paths. This skill guides performance analysis, report generation, and targeted optimization planning.
actual_capabilities: Detects bottlenecks across communication, processing, memory, and network areas.
Shows Claude Flow commands for bottleneck detection, profiling, reports, and monitoring.
Guides performance report creation for markdown, HTML, and JSON outputs.
Provides optimization recommendations for topology, caching, concurrency, priorities, and resources.
Includes CI workflow and custom script examples for recurring analysis.
limitations: Focuses on Claude Flow swarms and is not a general application profiler.
Recommendations depend on metrics available from Claude Flow commands.
Automatic fixes may change swarm behavior and should be reviewed before use.
Example scripts require Node.js, npx, and Claude Flow access.

use_cases.title: Diagnose slow swarm execution
use_cases.description: Find whether delays come from coordination, task queues, memory access, API latency, or agent utilization.

use_cases.title: Tune AI workflow throughput
use_cases.description: Use bottleneck reports to adjust topology, caching, concurrency, and priorities for Claude Flow workloads.

use_cases.title: Create performance review reports
use_cases.description: Generate recurring summaries that compare metrics, highlight regressions, and list prioritized improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic bottleneck check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the performance-analysis skill to identify current Claude Flow swarm bottlenecks. Summarize the highest impact issues and recommended next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a performance report
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a performance report for the last 24 hours. Include metrics, bottleneck impact, and prioritized recommendations in markdown.

prompt_templates.title: Compare swarm performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the current swarm with swarm-123. Highlight regressions, improvements, and actions that could improve throughput.

prompt_templates.title: Design continuous monitoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI and scheduled monitoring workflow for Claude Flow performance. Include thresholds, report outputs, and approval steps before any automatic fix.

output_examples.input: Analyze the current swarm for bottlenecks.
output_examples.output: A ranked report listing agent communication delay as the top issue, followed by task queue wait time and cache misses, with suggested fixes for each.
A summary with overall score, trend changes, key metrics, critical findings, and recommended work for the next optimization cycle.

output_examples.input: Review whether automatic fixes should be used.
output_examples.output: A change plan that separates safe recommendations from changes that need approval, backup, and rollback steps before execution.

best_practices: Run analysis before and after major topology or workload changes.
Export reports with timestamps so trends and regressions can be compared.
Review automatic fixes in a dry run or approval workflow before applying them.
anti_patterns: Running --fix on production swarms without reviewing planned changes.
Treating sample performance gains as guarantees for every workload.
Comparing reports from different time ranges without noting workload changes.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes Claude Flow swarm performance, including communication, processing, memory, network latency, and agent utilization.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill documents Claude Flow commands and examples. Command execution depends on the agent or user workflow that applies the skill.

faq.question: Can it fix bottlenecks?
faq.answer: It documents an optional --fix mode. Review proposed changes and use approval controls before applying fixes to active systems.

faq.question: What report formats are covered?
faq.answer: The guidance covers markdown, HTML, and JSON reports, including metrics, bottleneck impact, comparisons, and recommendations.

faq.question: Is this useful outside Claude Flow?
faq.answer: It is specialized for Claude Flow swarms. General profiling tools are better for unrelated applications or infrastructure.

faq.question: What access is needed?
faq.answer: Users need access to Claude Flow metrics, relevant swarm identifiers, and a writable location when exporting reports.
